title: Khronos MultipleScenes -- two scenes, and the file names which one a viewer opens with

criterion.says: For the first scene, the mesh is a triangle. For the second scene, the mesh is a square. The default scene is set to `1` by the `scene` property, so viewers should initially show the scene containing the square.
criterion.note: Numeric because the drawn coverage decides it outright: the square and the triangle occupy the same corner of space, so a reader that opened scene 0 draws exactly half this frame fraction in the same box.

acceptanceClass.because: A fronto-parallel planar placement owns three continuous freedoms -- two of aim and one of scale -- and every distinct silhouette line costs one condition, so 2 + k >= E is what decides whether the construction can be written at all (`board/`). The subject is Khronos's square, which is planar and has only four lines, so the count would permit the construction -- what stops it is that the case's whole criterion is WHICH scene the file's own `scene` property selects, and its camera comes from the framing rule over that scene's bounds. Moving it to a constructed placement is admissible and is not built; unlike the cases above, this one is pending rather than structural.

subjects.name: MultipleScenes
subjects.notes: Two scenes of one node each, two meshes, two buffers, no material and no uv. Scene 0 is a triangle and scene 1 is a square, and the document's `scene` property is 1. Khronos: 'The default scene is set to `1` by the `scene` property, so viewers should initially show the scene containing the square.' The criterion is therefore about WHICH geometry is drawn and not about how it is shaded, so the subject carries nothing that would shade it.

source.pinReason: the same pin every other Khronos subject in this tree carries

blender.note: A release version, not a commit. Recorded so a red rung can be attributed to our renderer or to the oracle, and carried in the oracle's cache key so a version bump misses instead of serving a stale render. We do not aim to be bit-identical with Cycles.

camera.derivation: The framing rule of board:0083 (src/gltf/Framing.h) applied to THE DEFAULT SCENE's own bounds, which is the point of the case: the square spans (0,0,0)..(1,1,0), so r = |max-min|/2 = 0.70710678118654757 m and the centre is (0.5, 0.5, 0). Azimuth 35 deg and elevation 20 deg in glTF's +Y-up frame, distance r / sin(yfov/2) / 0.6, yfov = 2*atan(12/50) from Blender's factory 50 mm lens on a 24 mm sensor height at sensor_fit VERTICAL, near = distance - r and far = distance + r. THE TRIANGLE OF SCENE 0 SPANS THE SAME BOX, so this camera does not by itself decide which scene is drawn -- it frames either one -- and the verdict rests on the silhouette rather than on the framing. The roll is zero and stated: a rolled axis-aligned square would be a different draw of the same lottery rather than an exactness argument.
camera.note: THE ENGINE'S OWN ANSWER, QUOTED (board:1398). Every number here is read from the framing rule's output for this subject -- eye, aim, yfov and both clip planes -- rather than recomputed by the authoring helper, which bounded each primitive by the eight transformed corners of its local AABB and therefore always at least as loosely as the engine bounds the transformed vertices. A looser radius moves the eye back, and 93 cases declared a camera the rule does not derive. `ADerivedCameraIsTheFramingRuleAndNotAQuotation` recomputes all of it and refuses a mismatch, so what this declaration does is PIN the viewpoint, never choose it.

light.note: The only illumination is Blender's factory world. A uniform environment is what makes a Lambertian facet return rho*L with no integration left.

world.note: Configured by not being configured. The observed colour and strength go into provenance.json, so a Blender that changed them is visible without any machinery that refuses.

material.note: The default scene is ONE unoccluded facet, which is the one shape where Cycles has no integration left and the answer is the closed form rho*L = 0.8 x 0.05087608844041824 = 0.0407008707523346. The file declares no material at all, so declaring one here takes nothing away from the asset: what it tests is which geometry a viewer opens with, and a colour cannot answer that.

default.note: One sample per pixel with the box filter at its RNA minimum makes Cycles evaluate the same predicate a centre-sampling rasteriser does, because the integer raster coordinate is the pixel centre and the sample never leaves +/-0.005 px of it.

notes: Khronos's criterion is the default scene and nothing else: 'viewers should initially show the scene containing the square'. The two scenes' meshes occupy the same corner of space, so the square and the triangle are told apart by their SILHOUETTE and not by their place -- a reader that opened scene 0 would draw half this coverage in the same box, which is why the frame fraction is declared and recomputed.

subjectFrameFraction.note: The fraction of the frame the subject's projected area covers at frame 0, RE-HARVESTED after the camera became the framing rule's own answer (board:1398). Recomputed by the runner on every run and refused on mismatch, so this line PINS the framing and never chooses it; seeded from that recomputation, it is a drift detector rather than a present-error check.
